category: multi-hoster / debrid (link unrestrict only, no torrent cache)

free_tier.stated: No free tier and no self-service signup: 'In order to obtain Elite Services, you must first submit the applicable application form ... to LinkSnappy for review and initial approval', which 'may include ... your credit card information'.
free_tier.notes: Prices are in the terms: 7-day trial 4.70 EUR, 30-day 12.50 EUR, 90-day 28.99 EUR, 180-day 52.99 EUR.

per_object_cap.stated: Not published; per-host data transfer limits exist ('Data transfer limits exist only on few hosts, rest are unlimited') and are shown on a status page behind a login.

retention.stated: No stored content to retain: links are generated on demand and 'We don't seed torrents after they've been downloaded.' Torrent support is absent altogether.

egress.terms: Generated links are IP-locked: 'The generated links are IP address locked and they will only work with the IP they were generated with', and 'if your IP changes after the downloading has begun, your download will fail since our system doesn't allow sharing of links among multiple people(IPs)'.

interface_detail: Web link generator plus browser plugins and download-manager integrations; the FAQ documents no public REST API, and https://linksnappy.com/api returned 404 on 2026-10-23.
tooling: browser extensions, JDownloader/IDM via the link generator, mobile app; no rclone backend found
chaining: The host-coverage specialist: 11 of 348 hosts in the comparison index, fewer than any other service there, but it reaches some obscure hosts the others drop, so it is a per-link fallback rather than a mount.

limits.value: every generated link is bound to the IP that generated it; a changed IP fails the download mid-transfer
per-host data transfer limits on 'a few hosts'; the rest are unlimited but the list is behind the login at /myaccount/status

limits_note: Two failure strings have no defined cause in the documentation: 'Error 503' and '087 Error' are listed as things to report, not as conditions a client can handle.
binding_note: The link dies with the address.

identity_cost.detail: An application reviewed by the vendor, with email and credit-card details supplied before approval; the terms allow denial 'at any time and for any reason'. Heavier than every other service in this set.

reliability_note: Links are IP-locked and a mid-transfer IP change fails the download; host support is the thinnest of the nine; the two most common errors ('Error 503', '087 Error') have no documented cause.
confidence_note: The IP-lock rule, the application gate and the prices are in the vendor's own FAQ and terms. The host count is the comparison index's, not the vendor's, and the vendor's own status page is behind a login.

notes: The gate is the earliest and the only one that can stop an account existing at all; the IP lock is the one that breaks a working account mid-download. Torrent support is absent, so the cache-behaviour question does not apply. The vendor's host status page requires a login and was not read. The legacy myaccount/news page still lists 2021-era cap upgrades (DDL 30->35 GB, Katfile 20->25 GB), which no longer matches the current 11-host table; The cheapest 7-day entry at US$4.99, and the most expensive 30 days at US$12.99, which is what 75+ hosts costs. Host-count claims conflict inside one site: 75+ (landing), 50 (FAQ), 11 rows (public status table). Flat for 37 months at USD 4.99 / 12.99 / 29.99 / 54.99, and the pricing model removes the promo-versus-renewal question entirely: every term is a one-off payment with 'No Recurring Payment'. The billed monthly rate is USD 12.99, at the highest 30-day entry price in the debrid set, against EUR 2.99-4.00 for the French services. The offer narrowed while the price did not: the FAQ answered 'Do you offer any free trials? Yes' in 2023-09 and the question is gone from 2024-10 onward, so a 37-month history that tracked only the dollar figure would have called this provider unchanged twice over. A proxy with a price, not a store. The terms and the FAQ agree, which makes this one of the cleanest zeroes. Search-engine extracts of the vendor's own checkout page (linksnappy.com/myaccount/extend) show the rail buttons 'Credit/Debit Card, Paysafecard, Bitcoin, Reseller' and linksnappy.com/landing shows 'CashtoCode Paysafecard Cryptocurrency'. No torrent support, which the comparison corpus and the FAQ both imply. A missing client is not a rejection and neither is a missing document: the API exists and answers, it is just not written down.

extras.failure_angle: IP-locked links and a human gate
extras.account_states: application denied; account suspended; expired membership (no renewal state documented)
extras.cache_miss: not applicable: no torrent cache and no stored content
extras.host_removal: 'There are instances where a host might stop working, we usually fix such issues quickly'; the live list is behind /myaccount/status
extras.simultaneous_use: Every generated link is bound to the generating IP and a mid-download IP change fails the transfer. The FAQ gives that as the anti-sharing mechanism rather than a login rule.
extras.annual_plan: none; 180 days is the longest term
extras.renewal: none: every term is a one-off payment, so there is no promo-to-renewal step
extras.free_tier_closed: a free trial was advertised on 2023-09-23 and is absent from 2024-10-07, 2025-10-01 and 2026-10-23

payment.paypal_note: 'If you still wish to pay via paypal you can visit one of our resellers and pay via them'
payment.voucher_detail: CashtoCode voucher (Funanga) redeemed at checkout; Paysafecard; resellers

extras.auth_flows: one, undocumented: AUTHENTICATE with account credentials returns a session key that later calls carry. No OAuth, no device code, no published token lifetime.
extras.account_endpoints: GET /api/USERDETAILS (the client comments that it 'Does not work well with cookies')
extras.public_endpoints_no_account: GET /api/REGEX; the host registry /api/FILEHOSTSREALTIME appears to want a session but was not probed
